distinguishing_features: Direct application of micro-oscillation via existing pitch actuator pressure control to prevent static friction locking
Software-only implementation using existing hydraulic system without new sensors or hardware
Continuous sub-lift micro-loading during idle to maintain dynamic interface state
Targeted elimination of fretting root cause (micro-slip under static load) through active vibration rather than passive resistance
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Preventing fretting corrosion in wind turbine pitch bearings during idle by eliminating static friction-induced micro-slip without adding hardware or relying on surface treatments
parsed.viable_reason: The mechanism uses feasible pressure modulation within existing hydraulic system capabilities to generate micro-oscillations that prevent static lock, validated by measurable flow and pressure signals.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The use of the pitch actuator's pressure loop for active micro-vibration to prevent fretting is not an obvious extension of prior monitoring or passive design approaches, as it repurposes control logic for a novel mechanical effect.
